payload.claim: Criterion 3's acceptance text and its own witness description require that an escape above U+10FFFF (the example given is `\UFFFFFFFF`) answers 400, but no test in tests/test_view_server.py ever sends such an escape. `test_sparql_refuses_a_service_clause_however_spelled`'s `queries` list covers SERVICE in various cases and two in-range escapes (`\u0053ERVICE`, `SERV\U00000049CE`) but nothing that exercises the `code_point > 0x10FFFF` branch. Changing `raise ValueError(...)` to `raise OverflowError(...)` on this line means the exception is no longer caught by `_handle_sparql`'s `except ValueError`, so a request with an out-of-range escape would propagate an unhandled exception instead of answering 400 - and the full test suite stays green because nothing drives that input.
